info.name: CalPlan
info.summary: Your calendar, sorted — automatically place flagged tasks into free slots
info.description:
CalPlan finds time for your Nextcloud tasks. Turn on **Auto-schedule** for a task and CalPlan adds a `🔒 Task title` time block to the first free place in your working hours. When you edit or finish the task, CalPlan updates or removes the block.
**Important setup:** put scheduled tasks in a calendar/list that supports **both tasks and events** (`VTODO` + `VEVENT`). A Tasks-only list cannot store CalPlan's event block, and Tasks-only calendars may not appear in third-party calendar apps. In Nextcloud Tasks, choose a normal calendar that supports tasks—not a Tasks-only list.
**How it works** 1. Open a task in Nextcloud Tasks and turn on **Auto-schedule** (or add the standard `calplan` tag from another CalDAV client). 2. CalPlan checks your calendars for busy time and finds a free block. Personal exclusions can completely remove selected calendars from CalPlan or make ordinary events with selected titles stop counting as busy. 3. It writes one derived event for that task. The task remains the source of truth: edit the task, not the calendar block. 4. Completing, cancelling, or untagging the task removes its block on the next reconcile.
Task start and due dates are respected. The default block is 30 minutes; set a standard iCalendar `DURATION`, or add a notes line such as `Duration: 15min` or `Duration: 1hr`. A `First step:` notes line is shown as `👣 First step:` in the slot; legacy `Next:` lines remain supported. Help buttons beside Reconcile and Auto-schedule explain these helpers.
After a task block ends, CalPlan can add a filterable `calplan-review` (“Is complete?”) task tag and either try another time or pause Auto-schedule, according to your personal setting. Personal limits can cap both task minutes and task-block count per day. Ignored calendars are completely outside CalPlan: their tasks, events, tags, and existing blocks are not read or changed. Ignored event-title rules are case-insensitive and can use exact or contains matching; they affect ordinary busy events only, never tasks or CalPlan blocks. The Reconcile help shows the latest run, while Personal settings keeps privacy-safe diagnostics for the latest ten runs. CalPlan is self-contained, uses standard iCalendar properties, and does not patch the Tasks or Calendar apps. Calendar changes are picked up by the background/on-demand reconcile; task edits reconcile immediately. Calendar clients refresh on their own sync interval, so you may need to press refresh to see a new or removed block right away.
